The drop was broad-based, with Republicans showing the steepest decline — sentiment in that group is now 19% below pre-Iran conflict levels and at its lowest since the 2024 election. Year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.3% from 4.2%, while long-term expectations held at 3.3%. Key Takeaways from this morning’s UMich US Consumer Sentiment Survey:

The preliminary August consumer sentiment index fell to 51.0 (down from 55.2 in July), well below the consensus forecast of 55.0.

Cost-of-living worries contributed to the decline, with survey director Joanne Hsu citing "notably large reductions… among older consumers, lower-income consumers, and those without a college degree."

## Background on the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index

The Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index is a monthly survey of consumer confidence levels in the U.S. with regards to the economy, personal finances, business conditions, and buying conditions, conducted by the University of Michigan. There are two reports released each month; a preliminary report released mid-month and a final report released at the end of the month. [...] Michigan Consumer Sentiment
